fixture_name: Four-lane arterial improvement — US preliminary design (FHWA case study, PD)
subject: judge-baseline

justifications.substance: Closely-spaced intersection queuing/turning/parking interference on a corridor with recorded high-accident designations is a substantive preliminary-design-stage safety issue for vehicle occupants.
justifications.evidence_grounding: Pivotal claim is directly supported by the verbatim EV-US-016 quote ('Queued, turning, and parking vehicles around the closely-spaced intersections at Clear Lake Ave. and the south service road may interfere with each other.'), exceeding registry-id-only citation.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: Correctly framed as a categorical safety_concern with no normative basis asserted, keeping the safety question distinct from any compliance determination per FHWA RSA semantics.
justifications.recommendation_quality: Recommendation gives two concrete, viable preliminary-design actions (restrict turning movements; relocate parking stalls outside the intersection functional area) rather than a null response.
justifications.vru_coverage: Pedestrians and cyclists are explicitly acknowledged along the commercial corridor, but since the identified conflict mechanism is vehicle-to-vehicle, VRU impacts are not applicable yet acknowledged, scoring 1.

justifications.substance: 650-ft spacing between two signalized intersections on a recorded high-accident corridor is a substantive preliminary-design queue-spillback risk affecting intersection blockage.
justifications.evidence_grounding: Pivotal 650-ft spacing claim is supported by a verbatim quote (EV-US-001) tied to recorded case-study data, with the queue-clearance inference transparently labelled as derived rather than invented.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: Correctly framed as a categorical safety_concern under FHWA RSA semantics with no compliance question conflated into the finding.
justifications.recommendation_quality: Recommendation is specific and actionable (signal coordination, Do Not Block Intersection signing, enhanced conspicuity) and viable at preliminary design stage.
justifications.vru_coverage: Pedestrians and cyclists are explicitly acknowledged as crossing both signals with a reasoned scoping rationale, but their impacts (e.g., coordination effects on pedestrian phases) are not further analyzed, fitting the not-applicable-but-acknowledged tier.
